# K8.8 Philox4x32-7 for NVFP4 stochastic rounding

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Build option: `NVTE_BUILD_NUM_PHILOX_ROUNDS=7` (`nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/Dockerfile` L117, no run-time
switch) · Class: **Not equivalent** (different random bits) · Rule basis: open, see section 9

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

| | G6, G6b, G6c |
|---|---|
| Build option | `NVTE_BUILD_NUM_PHILOX_ROUNDS=7` in the TE build step (`nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/Dockerfile` L106-120, option at L117) |
| Recorded in | `firmus_gb300_ngpu8_gptoss_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2_nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2.json` L22; `nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/README_nvfp4_v7.md` L10, L40; `../KERNELS.md` Summary row 8.8 |
| Code | none; an option of the TE build |

Both packages use the same `Dockerfile`, and so does G6c. G3 builds TE without the option.

## 2. What the reference does

NVIDIA's gpt-oss-20b recipe builds TE without this option
(`nemo_g1_1012/Dockerfile` L65), so TE's default round count applies; `../KERNELS.md` section 2 gives
it as 10 (TE's CMake source is not in the package). TE draws the stochastic-rounding bits of its
NVFP4 casts (the gradient quantizers of the recipe, `NVTE_NVFP4_DISABLE_STOCHASTIC_ROUNDING=0`,
config L168) from a Philox4x32 counter-based generator with that many rounds.

For comparison only: NVIDIA's llama31_8b reference Dockerfile, kept unchanged in
`llama31_8b/implementations/nemo_l1_1012/Dockerfile` L67 (README L7, L10), builds
TE with `NVTE_BUILD_NUM_PHILOX_ROUNDS=3`. That is another benchmark's reference and not a ruling.

## 3. What this implementation does

The image's TE is built with 7 Philox rounds. Every stochastically rounded NVFP4 cast in TE uses
the 7-round stream; scales, amaxes and round-to-nearest outputs do not use random bits. The
Triton activation cast with its own Philox (`NVFP4_TRITON_SR_ROUNDS`, default 10, V7 patch
L384-386) is not enabled.

## 4. Why the result is the same, or what changes

The stochastically rounded data bytes come from a different random stream, so training is not
bit-identical to a 10-round build: **Not equivalent**. The rounding rule is unchanged: each
value rounds up with probability equal to its fractional position between the two neighbouring
FP4 values. Philox4x32-7 is reported to pass the BigCrush suite (Salmon et al., SC 2011,
`../KERNELS.md` section 8.8); the paper is not in the package. The test below measures
the rounding statistics of the 7-round build; it does not compare with a 10-round build.

## 5. Numerics

Only the random bits change; formats, scales, amax and the RHT are as in K2.1.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** compile time; applies to every TE NVFP4 cast with stochastic rounding.
- **Falls back:** none; there is no run-time way back to 10 rounds in the image.
- **Assumes:** that 7 rounds give random bits of sufficient quality for stochastic rounding.
  Not checked at run time; evidence is the test statistics below and the cited literature.
- **Check:** `nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/Dockerfile` L117; `firmus_gb300_ngpu8_gptoss_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2_nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2.json` L22.
- **Records available on request** (not in the package): the image build log
  (of the G6b image; the `Dockerfile` is the same) shows the option in the executed command. Image verify jobs 22541 and 22589 on the G6b image (same patches and `Dockerfile`; not repeated on this image):
  `OK quantize outputs bitwise equal to ph7 (r7) library`: 84 output tensors of NVFP4 quantize
  calls, including stochastic-rounding cases (`rowcol_rht_sr`, `col_rht_sr`), equal to those of a
  7-round TE library built in the development repository.

## 7. Code

`nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/Dockerfile` L117 (step 4, L106-120). No Firmus source.

## 8. Tests and evidence

- **Kernel test on the image** (Firmus test script `k8_8_sr_stats.py`, available on request),
  job 22445, runs a and b rc 0, 93 cases per run (G6 image; on this package's image job 22899: 121 cases per run, 44 with a difference, run a vs b 59 equal, 42 differ).
  TE `NVFP4Quantizer` row-wise, no RHT.
  - Statistics (test `k8_8_sr_stats`, job 22235): blocks with amax 6 (decode scale 1),
    other elements 1 + 0.5 f, 15 728 640 elements per f, 9 values of f from 1/64 to 63/64. Share
    rounded up vs f: largest deviation 1.3e-4 (f = 0.75), at most 1.2 binomial standard
    deviations √(f(1 − f)/N). Largest |signed mean error| 6.4e-5. Share equal in two calls vs
    1 − 2f(1 − f) for independent draws: largest deviation 3.8e-4. Only the values 1 and 1.5
    occur; 3 digests in 3 repeats; round to nearest gives one value per f.
  - 30 cases with a difference per run, all by design: SR call 1 vs call 2 and RTN vs SR data on
    seeded, zero-block, saturating, special-value and 7 captured MLP inputs (captured inputs:
    about 18.8 M and 14.7 M elements). Scale and amax RTN vs SR: 0 differ, except widths 2032
    and 2064 with 1024 and 3065 scale entries. Those widths have 127 and 129 scale columns,
    padded to 128 and 132 (1024 and 3072 padding entries for 1024 rows), consistent with
    unwritten padding, not values.
  - Run a vs run b: 45 equal, 28 differ, all SR data comparisons.
- **Convergence:** the 10 scored runs of each package were made with this build.

## 9. Open points

1. Rule question: the rules name stochastic rounding as a numerically safe technique (TR-5.2b)
   and do not name a random number generator or round count. Whether a reduced Philox round
   count is covered by that, or needs a ruling, is open.
2. No test compares the statistics of the 7-round build with a 10-round build of the same TE
   commit in the package image.
3. The BigCrush statement rests on the cited paper; the package has no copy or excerpt.
